## Analysis

Sol_0026 shows that coupled row–column cross reconstruction also cannot escape the `q=56` tensor plateau. Combined with sol_0024–0025, this refutes cell, slice, and moderate two-axis mask moves; the 277-cell support is locally optimized within the tensor parameterization. Geometry changes alone previously failed, but those searches retained the same cell support. The remaining promising direction is to abandon exact tensor membership while using sol_0023’s emitted one-dimensional set as a seed: its additive collisions may survive coordinated coordinate perturbations that create new sums faster than differences.

## Next

Embed sol_0023 as an atomic fallback, then run a 155-second parallel-tempering search directly on its 277 integer coordinates, using seed `5027`, range `[0,4000]`, and mutations comprising 50% single-point displacement (`±1..32`), 30% contiguous rank-block displacement (2–16 points), and 20% equal-and-opposite displacement of two blocks; canonicalize translations/GCD, enforce distinctness and `220<=n<=340`, exact-score candidates, and checkpoint strict improvements.
